Checkers on NoCharge — mandatory captures and the simple rule

The current Checkers game uses English-draughts movement, compulsory jumps, and a stated simple-capture rule. Here is what the V2 engine accepts—and what it does not.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

English draughts for two, one device.

Play CheckersBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: NoCharge Checkers is an eight-by-eight, two-player English-draughts game. Captures are compulsory when available, but the engine does not require the capture line that takes the most pieces. If a jumped piece can jump again, the same piece must continue until no further jump is available.

The capture rule

The game checks for legal jumps across the board. If at least one exists for the active player, a quiet diagonal move is not accepted. When more than one jump is legal, the player may choose among those legal jumps; there is no longest-chain or “capture the most” requirement in the current engine.

After a jump, the same piece remains selected when another capture is available. The turn changes only when the chain has no further legal jump. This is continuation, not an option to stop midway.

Movement and promotion

Uncrowned men move and capture one square diagonally forward. Kings move one square diagonally in either direction; they do not slide across several squares. Reaching the far row crowns a man. The current game ends when the other player has no pieces or no legal move.

Controls and current source

Tap a piece and a highlighted destination, or use the row and column controls. The current player and legal destinations are stated on the board. Check the Checkers page for the live controls and reset behavior. This page describes the shipped V2 rules, not every national draughts variant.
